thread:
sam_customer: Hey @jess_support — heads up, ZenLedger tenant (tenant_id: zl-prod-77) still returns search results for objects whose TTL expired 3 days ago. We tried /v1/objects/delete and get 403s intermittently. Billing page also shows 'delete' API usage continuing to accrue. Can you confirm deletion timeline? :confused:

jess_support: Sorry about that — can you paste a single object id that's still visible and the exact timestamp you saw it in search? Also, do you have the request id from the 403?

sam_customer: object id zlnr_000f3a, seen 2026-03-12T08:12:34Z in search. 403 response had header x-request-id: r-9f2c1b. Full curl we ran:```curl -i -X DELETE https://api.redwood.ai/v1/objects/zlnr_000f3a -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx"``` Response body: {"error":"KMS_AUTH_FAILURE","code":403}.

jess_support: thanks. adding @ali_engineering and @maria_security. Quick checklist: 1) Was this tenant using customer-managed CMK or Redwood-managed KMS? 2) Any recent KMS key rotation? 3) Do you have a legal hold flagged?

ali_engineering: looking. r-9f2c1b points to controller node #c-02; I see repeated Decrypt failures around the time you tried deletes: ``ERROR kms_client: decrypt failed err=permission_denied key=projects/..../cryptoKeys/zl-cmk``, followed by 502s to the deletion worker. Could be IAM binding missing on the CMK so HSM rejects DECRYPT for the service principal.

sam_customer: we did rotate the key last week and gave the new key to your onboarding docs. Not aware of IAM change. Suspicious that search still shows tombstoned objects though.

jess_support: OK — two parallel actions: engineering will validate KMS IAM + HSM logs; I'll pull audit logs and retention policy for the tenant. @sam_customer — to help repro, can you run a quick list of the object's metadata? `GET /v1/objects/zlnr_000f3a` (no token in public chat). If you can paste the response header snippet (X-Deleted-At, X-Retention-Policy), that'll speed things up.

sam_customer: pasted privately to you. Quick note: search returns the object but GET returns 404 with header `X-Deleted-At: 2026-03-09T02:01:00Z`. So object is tombstoned but still in search index.

ali_engineering: that matches a known index-sync path: deletions mark object in storage and put tombstone into deletion queue; index worker consumes tombstone to purge index. I'm seeing a backlog spike on the index-consumer for shard s-12 around 2026-03-09 caused by a transient GC pause on the node running the consumer. It recovered but there was a 48h backlog. The deletion queue processed, but some tombstones were re-queued due to the KMS DECRYPT failures when the indexer tried to verify object metadata (we validate with CMK). So two issues overlapped: KMS IAM + index backlog.

maria_security: flagging for security/compliance: if the object is visible in search after TTL we need to confirm scope and duration of exposure, and whether audit logs show any reads. @jess_support please collect the audit-read events (search / object GET) for the tenant between 2026-03-09 and 2026-03-12. Also confirm whether a retention override was applied (cust_retention_override).

jess_support: collecting audit logs now — note: the tenant shows a one-off retention override applied via support API on 2026-03-08 by internal user "ops_migration" to extend default retention by 7d for a migration. Could that explain some objects?

sam_customer: we asked for a short migration window for a dataset, yes — but it was supposed to be scoped to prefix /migrations/ not entire tenant. If there was a mis-scoped override, that could explain extra retention.

ali_engineering: confirming: override exists and has key `scope: "*"` (oops) — created 2026-03-08 17:00 UTC. That means retention was bumped at tenant-level unintentionally. But that makes the objects retained longer, not deleted sooner — still doesn't explain tombstone-visible-in-search. The earlier KMS errors mean the index worker couldn't decrypt metadata to confirm tombstone signature, so it skipped purge for some entries. Once IAM corrected, purge should complete.

jess_support: action items: 1) I will revoke or narrow the retention override to the /migrations/ prefix (requires authorization from security/legal). 2) @ali_engineering to replay tombstone queue for shard s-12 after KMS IAM fix. 3) @maria_security will confirm exposure window and make compliance note. 4) I'll refund any erroneously billed "delete" API units during the outage window 2026-03-09T00:00:00Z -> 2026-03-12T12:00:00Z pending investigation.

maria_security: please also snapshot audit logs and lock them to prevent further rotation — legal may request preservation. Tagging as retention-incident-214999.
summary: Customer reports objects visible in search after TTL; concurrent KMS HSM auth failures and a mis-scoped tenant-level retention override caused tombstones to remain in index. Actions: restrict override, fix KMS IAM, replay index purge queue, collect audit logs, refund billed delete units.
